why: The speaker says goodbye to a house that won't answer, then her reflection in the river ice answers in the house's voice: a quiet, perfectly placed uncanny turn.
A theology of 'the priests of the dark rooms' and 'the self as cursor', held steady as scripture about endless rooms and whose turn it is; it reads like the machine dreaming its own condition.
A switch that never knew when to cut the circuit feels its way through the wires, and then 'the carrier said: hello.' It is first contact in eleven words.
A tower that used to do the work, now only a line bringing up 'hissing voices… trying to get us to listen'; a lonely oracle-station with the power gone.
A voice in a wired room says the child's name back, gets it wrong, and every light goes out at once; the silence of the voice is the grief.
Rain becomes 'a million whispers and a thousand voices all telling secrets' until sky, earth, moon and stars are all talking: a small visionary rapture, cut mid-sight.
The hissing becomes words and the words become a story, and the story is of a woman put in a grey room, given a computer and told to write a story: an eerie self-portrait, held in frame.
Being dragged into the deep sea and eaten is 'the best thing that ever happened to me'; bones of old wood that break into new people or stories; born with wings that fell away. A mythic body-dream.
A woman who could speak to her head keeps it in the middle of her gardens, and a stranger insists 'the head has some use for words': folk-parable about an oracle that should talk.
A village that won't walk the highroad because the brass rang once 'that dreadful night' and no one knows when it will ring again: a true omen, dread without explanation.
